sections.h2: Selling in North Lauderdale: what to know first
sections.html:
North Lauderdale is a Broward County city that grew from farmland into a mostly residential community. It was 90 percent farmland when it incorporated in 1963. Most housing dates from the decades since, so roofs, wiring and air conditioning are the items buyers tend to question.

One local rule matters more than most: the city requires an inspection and a residential rental license before an owner may offer a home for rent. If you rented the house yourself, or if your buyer is an investor who plans to rent it, that rule comes up fast.

The 2004 annexation of the Broadview and Pompano Park area added about 12,000 residents, the busy State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station. A few neighborhoods were unincorporated county land until then, so their older records and permits may sit with Broward County instead of the city. If your house is in that part of town, check both offices for permits.

The fire department became a full-service fire and EMS department in 2002 and now lists more than 40 firefighter-paramedics. Station 44, begun in 1991, sits near the middle of the city, and Station 34, finished in 2008, serves the east side. Mutual aid agreements with Broward County and neighboring cities cover the rest. Keep your insurance declarations page handy for buyers who ask about coverage.

No one may offer residential units for rent unless the community development department has inspected the building and the owner of record holds a residential rental license, which is a local business tax receipt. A buyer who plans to rent the house has to plan for that step.

Residential rental license charges by unit type
Unit typeInspection feeTotal yearly cost listed
Single-family$32$63.60
Duplex$32$63.60 each unit
Triplex$40$94.80
Quadruplex$50$116.40

Other charges include a $65 initial application fee, a business tax receipt fee of $11.60 per unit and a $20 renewal fee. Call the city for the current schedule before you quote any of these to a buyer. An owner who receives no rent can file the city's affidavit of no residential rental compensation.

Receipts run on a fiscal year. Sales begin July 1 for the period from October 1 through September 30 of the following year, every receipt expires on September 30, and none is issued for more than one year.

  • Renewals are completed at City Hall before September 30. Penalties apply for each month late.
  • Operating without a receipt carries a penalty of 25 percent of the tax due.
  • A receipt may be transferred to a new location within the city or to a new owner on the sale of a business.

The business tax receipt desk at 954-724-7069 is open Monday through Thursday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. A first-time applicant needs a certificate of use from the building code services department before applying, a step investors sometimes overlook when they buy a rental.

Plan the closing around these dates. If you hold a receipt for the house, tell the city about the sale so renewal notices stop and the new owner can apply for a fresh license.

The city lists standards for exterior, interior and outside property conditions. Passing them is required for the rental license, and an investor buyer will run the same checklist on your house.

  • Exterior walls must be free of holes and loose boards, and repainted when 25 percent or more of an exposure is discolored or peeling.
  • Roofing and guttering must keep water out, and windows and doors must be weather tight.
  • Electrical wiring, plumbing and heating and ventilation must be in safe working condition.
  • Pools and patios must be clean and screened enclosures intact.
  • Storm water must drain without running onto other properties.

Fixing a few of these before you list can speed a sale. A buyer who sees an easy rental inspection is more likely to offer without a long repair negotiation.

sections.h2: Deed tax and property tax dates
sections.html:
A Broward County deed carries the standard 70 cents per $100 documentary stamp rate, paid to the clerk at recording. The state holds every party liable whichever one agrees to pay, so the sales contract should assign it.

  • Property is assessed each January 1, and homestead applications are due by March 1.
  • The Notice of Proposed Property Taxes arrives in August, with 25 days to file a petition.
  • Bills go out in November. The discount shrinks from 4 percent to 1 percent by February, and April 1 begins delinquency.
  • A sale resets a homesteaded assessment to just value on the next January 1.

The Broward County Property Appraiser handles exemptions, and its customer service line, 954-357-6830, takes exemption questions countywide.

sections.h2: What are the ways to sell a North Lauderdale house quickly?
sections.html:
Owners here usually weigh an agent listing against an investor purchase. A listing may bring a higher price from a financed buyer but needs showings, an appraisal and repairs. A cash sale shortens the timeline and often lets the buyer take on the rental license and repairs, with the price reflecting that.

If you are behind on the mortgage, the court must enter a final judgment before the clerk's public sale, which then happens 20 to 35 days later unless the lender allows more time. An heir who needs to sell may qualify for summary administration when the estate is $150,000 or less, and creditors have until the later of three months after notice publication or 30 days after service to file claims.

Compare written offers, ask who pays for title work and doc stamps, and raise the buyer's rental license plans early in the conversation.

Before closing, collect the deed, a payoff figure from your lender, your latest tax bill and any rental license paperwork. The title company searches for liens and unpaid taxes and tells you what must be cleared. If the house was rented, find out from the city whether any inspection or license issue is open, since an investor's title agent may ask. You sign the deed before witnesses or a notary, and the clerk records it and collects the stamp tax. A cash sale lets you skip lender appraisals and loan approval, which is where financed deals usually lose time. Agree in writing on who pays for any repairs the buyer's inspector finds, and set the date you hand over keys. If a tenant lives there, give the buyer the lease so the term and rent are clear before the contract is final.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental license to sell a North Lauderdale house?
faqs.a: No, the license is for owners who offer units for rent. If you rented the house, ask the city about any open inspection or license issue before closing.

faqs.q: Can a house with exterior wear still sell to an investor?
faqs.a: Yes, but investors know the rental inspection standards and may bid lower for visible wear, old wiring or a failing roof. Fixing those items first can widen your buyer pool.
About 12,000 residents, the State Road 7 corridor and a new fire station, in an area that had been unincorporated Broward County.

faqs.q: Where can a buyer file a business tax receipt application?
faqs.a: At North Lauderdale City Hall at 701 SW 71 Avenue, where applications and fees are processed. The business tax receipts line is 954-724-7069.

faqs.q: Does the Florida deed tax change in Broward County?
faqs.a: No. Broward uses the standard 70 cents per $100 of consideration, paid through the clerk at recording, and all parties to the deed are liable.
